messages:
secops: EDR alert triggered for device macbook-pro-olivia (user: olivia) — detection: PUA.Mac.UnwantedInstaller. Quarantined file /Users/olivia/Downloads/installer.pkg and terminated process InstallerHelper PID 8421. Can the owner confirm this is expected?
EDR-bot: [automated] Alert ID: edr-20260305-8843. Actions taken: quarantine, process kill, file hash recorded (sha256=3b7f...c9e). Initial network indicators: outbound to telemetry.vendor-example.com:443.
olivia: that's my laptop — I installed something this morning (homebrew cask). I don't remember an installer.pkg. I'll stop any further installs. Please advise next steps.
it-support: @olivia if you can, please don't reboot. We can start a remote session and pull sysdiagnose + EDR logs. Ping me when you're free (I have a slot in 10m).
raj: quick triage checklist: 1) preserve logs (EDR + system) 2) capture `spctl --status` and `mdls /Users/olivia/Downloads/installer.pkg` 3) check `lsof -i` for active network connections from InstallerHelper.
secops: Adding: capture /var/log/install.log and output of `sudo opensnoop -n InstallerHelper` if still running. If it was signed, note the signing authority. Also set temp RBAC restriction — revoking local admin on the device until we confirm (we'll do via MDM).
EDR-bot: Full scan completed. No persistence artifacts found in LaunchAgents/LaunchDaemons. Sandbox scan: flagged strings matching known adware installer families. Network domains: telemetry.vendor-example.com (ASN 39520). File reputation: low confidence (heuristic-based).
maria: I'll pull cloud audit logs for the timeframe. We should encrypt the collected artifacts with KMS before uploading to the investigation bucket. Use key `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/ci-olivia-2026` and place objects under `s3://redwood-sec-inv/1778204123/`. cloud-audit-bot will post the CloudTrail event IDs.
cloud-audit-bot: Events found: CreateProcess on macOS (recorded via fleet telemetry) ts=2026-03-05T14:02:10Z eventId=evt-0a1b2c3d; NetworkConnect to telemetry.vendor-example.com ts=2026-03-05T14:02:12Z eventId=evt-0a1b2c3e. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-sec-inv/1778204123/ (server-side-encrypted with KMS key ci-olivia-2026).
olivia: remote session now. It-support, you can take over.
it-support: connected. running: `sudo sysdiagnose -f /tmp/sysdiag.olivia.tgz` and pulling EDR export.
secops: preliminary conclusion: likely a PUA bundled by a third-party cask; not a targeted compromise. Network calls appear to be telemetry to vendor, but we've quarantined the file and revoked local admin. If anyone sees anomalous cross-account access, escalate.
raj: action item: add a detection rule to reduce false positives for this vendor (signature tuning) and add a watch for any similar hashes. I'll file a short JIRA.
maria: post-incident steps: 1) audit S3 bucket access logs (CloudTrail) 2) ensure artifacts are KMS-encrypted and retention set to 90d 3) update onboarding doc to remind engineers to use approved MDM-approved installers.
secops: resolution: device cleaned, quarantined artifact remains in evidence bucket (KMS-encrypted), local admin temporarily revoked, detection signature ticket created (JIRA SEC-4532). Marking thread resolved pending JIRA and doc updates. :white_check_mark:
olivia: thanks everyone. appreciated the quick help. :thumbsup:
secops: we should also schedule a short retro in monday triage; add to agenda: adjust RBAC for dev machines and tighten cask installs.
